userStories.title: Permission catalog and entry grammar
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Add the code-owned permission catalog and pure entry expansion grammar under apps/api/src/permissions.

**Motivation** — Roles and bindings must exist, and be manageable, before any check can move onto them.

**Approach** — Catalog

`apps/api/src/permissions/catalog.ts` exports `PERMISSION_CATALOG: readonly PermissionCatalogEntry[]` and `findCatalogEntry(key: string): PermissionCatalogEntry | undefined`.

**Keys:**
- Every key in the `proposed_key` column of `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-18-permission-action-inventory.tsv`. A cell may hold several keys separated by `;`.
- Plus these new keys:
  - `role.read`, `role.manage`
  - `role.binding.manage`, `role.binding.global`, `role.binding.owner`
  - `approval.decide`, `approval.policy.read`, `approval.policy.manage`
  - `audit.read`
  - `memory.update`

**How fields are derived.** Rules apply in order; the first match decides `access`.

| Rule | Keys | `access` | `scope` | `ownable` |
|:--|:--|:--|:--|:--|
| 1 | key starts with `runner.` | `runner` | `any` | false |
| 2 | key starts with `system.` | `system` | `any` | false |
| 3 | `PUBLIC_KEYS`: `session.login`, `session.refresh`, `auth.register`, `auth.registration.read`, `health.read`, `invite.preview`, `invite.accept` | `public` | `any` | false |
| 4 | `IMPLICIT_KEYS`: `auth.me.read`, `session.logout`, `home.read`, `notification.read`, `notification.mark-read`, `notification.preference.read`, `notification.preference.update`, `agent.self.read`, `assistant.action.read`, `mcp.access` | `implicit` | `any` | false |
| 5 | every other key | `role` | see below | key is in `OWNABLE_KEYS` |

**Scope for `role` keys.**
- Keys in `OWNABLE_KEYS` take `any`.
- For other keys, take every TSV row of the key:
  - a row whose `catalog_scope` is `runner` counts as `global` (these are the admin runner routes, such as `fleet.runner.update`);
  - rows whose `catalog_scope` is `system`, `public` or `implicit` are ignored.

  Then:
- only `project` rows → `project`;
- only `global` rows → `global`;
- a mix of `project` and `global`, or any `own (see design §1)` row → `any`.

New keys take `global`, except `role.binding.manage`, `approval.decide` and `approval.policy.read`, which take `project`, and `approval.policy.manage`, which takes `any`. `memory.update` is in `OWNABLE_KEYS`, so it takes `any`.

The TSV `own (see design §1)` rows for `memory.create`, `memory.extract`, `memory.decision.record` and `thread.workspace.create` are **not** ownable: they create new rows, so there is no owner to compare. They take `any` under the rule above. `thread.workspace.read` is ownable on purpose, so a principal can be limited to reading its own workspace threads.

**`OWNABLE_KEYS`:**
- `comment.update`, `comment.delete`, `ticket.link.remove`, `memory.update`, `kb.document.delete`;
- `thread.cap.update`, `thread.plan`, `thread.run`, `thread.stop`, `thread.end-session`, `thread.answer`, `thread.archive`, `thread.publish`, `thread.discard`, `thread.message.send`;
- `thread.workspace.read`, `thread.workspace.message.send`, `thread.workspace.archive`.

**Other fields:**
- `risk`, decided by the first rule that matches:
  - `critical` for `role.*` and `approval.policy.*`, so `role.read` is `critical`;
  - `low` for keys whose last segment is `read`;
  - `high` for keys whose last segment is `delete` or `remove`, and for keys under `vcs.connection.`, `vcs.webhook-secret.`, `webhook.`, `fleet.repo.`, `fleet.runner.`, `fleet.budget.`, `fleet.enrollment.` and `fleet.credential.`;
  - `medium` otherwise.
- `principals`: `['user']` for `role.binding.owner`; `['user', 'agent']` otherwise.
- `approval`: `{ approvable: false, floor: 'none', default: 'none' }` when `access` is not `role` or `risk` is `low`; otherwise `{ approvable: true, floor: 'none', default: 'none' }`.

### Entry grammar and `expandEntries`

- A key **fits** a role scope when its `scope` is the same (`global` ↔ `GLOBAL`, `project` ↔ `PROJECT`) or is `any`.
- A key is **role-grantable** when its `access` is `role`.
- The output set holds plain keys, `X.own` strings, and `approval.decide@<pattern>` strings.

| Entry | Expands to |
|:--|:--|
| `k` (exact) | `k`, if `k` is role-grantable and fits. If `k` is not in the catalog: `UnknownPermissionEntryError`. If it is in the catalog but not role-grantable, or does not fit: `ScopeMismatchEntryError`. |
| `k.own` | `k.own`, if `k` is in `OWNABLE_KEYS` and fits. Otherwise the same errors as an exact entry. |
| `p.*` | every role-grantable, fitting key that starts with `p.`. Zero matches: `UnknownPermissionEntryError`. |
| `p.*.own` | `k.own` for every ownable, fitting key that starts with `p.`. Zero matches: `UnknownPermissionEntryError`. |
| `*` | every role-grantable, fitting key |
| `*.read` | every role-grantable, fitting key whose last segment is `read` |
| `approval.decide@<pattern>` | the string itself, where `<pattern>` is an exact key or `p.*` that matches at least one catalog key. Otherwise `UnknownPermissionEntryError`. |
| `!e` | removes from the result everything `e` expands to. All exclusions apply after all inclusions. |

A key `k` in the set implies `k.own` when checking (see `PermissionService.can`).

**Scope** — In: catalog.ts, entry-matcher.ts, exported OWNABLE_KEYS/IMPLICIT_KEYS/PUBLIC_KEYS, pure unit behavior. Out: schema/seeding (US-002), permission evaluation and ownership decisions (US-003), lifecycle wiring (US-004), APIs (US-005/006), approval enforcement.

**Interface** —
```ts
export type ApprovalMode = 'none' | 'self' | 'agent' | 'human';
export type KeyScope = 'global' | 'project' | 'any';
export interface PermissionCatalogEntry {
  key: string;                               // resource.verb[.qualifier]
  scope: KeyScope;
  access: 'role' | 'implicit' | 'public' | 'runner' | 'system';
  risk: 'low' | 'medium' | 'high' | 'critical';
  principals: readonly ('user' | 'agent')[];
  ownable: boolean;
  approval: { approvable: boolean; floor: ApprovalMode; default: ApprovalMode }; // placeholders until phase P3
}
export class UnknownPermissionEntryError extends Error { constructor(readonly entry: string) { super(entry); } }
export class ScopeMismatchEntryError extends Error { constructor(readonly entry: string) { super(entry); } }
export function expandEntries(entries: readonly string[], roleScope: 'GLOBAL' | 'PROJECT'): ReadonlySet<string>;
```
acceptanceCriteria: [unit] For every key in the proposed_key column of docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-18-permission-action-inventory.tsv split on ';', findCatalogEntry(key) returns an entry with that key.

routing.reasoning: Two pure source files implement a fully specified deterministic catalog and matcher without integration dependencies; medium complexity suffices, while access-control semantics require the security three-session-tdd override.

expandEntries(['notification.read'], 'GLOBAL') throws ScopeMismatchEntryError with entry 'notification.read'.
findCatalogEntry('memory.create').ownable returns false and its scope is 'any'.
findCatalogEntry('thread.workspace.read').ownable returns true and its scope is 'any'.
findCatalogEntry('role.read').approval returns { approvable: true, floor: 'none', default: 'none' }.

userStories.title: Role and RoleBinding schema, migration and system role seeder
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Persist roles and bindings and bootstrap the eleven system roles through a private repository layer and global module shell.

**Motivation** — Roles and bindings must exist, and be manageable, before any check can move onto them.

**Approach** — Schema
```prisma
/// Permissions P1a: a named set of permission entries.
model Role {
  id          String   @id @default(cuid())
  key         String   @unique // kebab-case, e.g. 'project-admin'
  name        String
  description String   @default("")
  scope       String   // GLOBAL | PROJECT
  system      Boolean  @default(false)
  locked      Boolean  @default(false)
  permissions Json     // string[] of entries
  createdAt   DateTime @default(now())
  updatedAt   DateTime @updatedAt

  bindings RoleBinding[]
}

/// Permissions P1a: a role given to a user or an agent, in one project or globally (projectId null).
model RoleBinding {
  id            String   @id @default(cuid())
  principalType String   // USER | AGENT
  principalId   String
  roleId        String
  projectId     String?
  grantedByType String   // USER | AGENT | SYSTEM
  grantedById   String
  createdAt     DateTime @default(now())

  role    Role     @relation(fields: [roleId], references: [id], onDelete: Restrict)
  project Project? @relation(fields: [projectId], references: [id], onDelete: Cascade)

  @@index([principalType, principalId])
  @@index([projectId])
  @@index([roleId])
}
```
- **`Project` back-relation.** `model Project` gains `roleBindings RoleBinding[]`.
- **Migration.** `apps/api/prisma/migrations/20261027090000_role_bindings/migration.sql` creates both tables and ships these two statements verbatim. The same strings are appended to `PARTIAL_UNIQUE_INDEXES` in `apps/api/test/helpers/partial-indexes.ts`.
```sql
CREATE UNIQUE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS "RoleBinding_principalId_roleId_projectId_key" ON "RoleBinding" ("principalType", "principalId", "roleId", "projectId") WHERE "projectId" IS NOT NULL
CREATE UNIQUE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS "RoleBinding_principalId_roleId_global_key" ON "RoleBinding" ("principalType", "principalId", "roleId") WHERE "projectId" IS NULL
```
- **Principal deletion.** `principalId` has no foreign key, because it points at a `User` or an `Agent`.
  - Agent deletion (`AgentsService.remove(slug)`, behind `DELETE /agents/:slug`) calls `MembershipService.removeAllBindings({ type: 'AGENT', id })`.
  - Users are never deleted, only disabled. Their bindings stay, and later readers check `disabled`.

### Seeded system roles
`apps/api/src/permissions/system-roles.ts` exports `SYSTEM_ROLES`. Each role has `system: true`; only `owner` also has `locked: true`.

| key | name | scope | permissions |
|:--|:--|:--|:--|
| `owner` | Owner | GLOBAL | `*` |
| `admin` | Admin | GLOBAL | `*`, `!role.binding.owner` |
| `member` | Member | GLOBAL | `agent.read`, `thread.workspace.read.own`, `thread.workspace.create`, `thread.workspace.message.send.own`, `thread.workspace.archive.own` |
| `agent` | Agent | GLOBAL | `agent.read` |
| `project-admin` | Project Admin | PROJECT | `*`, `approval.decide`, `approval.policy.manage` |
| `developer` | Developer | PROJECT | `*.read`, `ticket.create`, `ticket.update`, `ticket.assign`, `ticket.transition.*`, `ticket.label.*`, `ticket.link.add`, `ticket.link.remove.own`, `ticket.watch.*`, `comment.create`, `comment.update.own`, `comment.delete.own`, `label.create`, `label.update`, `agent.pickup`, `fleet.job.*`, `fleet.schedule.*`, `fleet.ticket-job.*`, `fleet.approval.decide.bash`, `fleet.knowledge.repo.reindex`, `thread.create`, `thread.*.own`, `kb.document.add`, `kb.document.delete.own`, `kb.search`, `memory.create`, `memory.extract`, `memory.decision.record`, `memory.update.own`, `codeintel.*`, `context.*` |
| `reviewer` | Reviewer | PROJECT | `*.read`, `comment.create`, `comment.update.own`, `comment.delete.own`, `ticket.transition.verify-fix.*`, `ticket.transition.close`, `agent.pickup`, `approval.decide` |
| `verifier` | Verifier | PROJECT | `*.read`, `comment.create`, `comment.update.own`, `comment.delete.own`, `ticket.transition.verify`, `ticket.transition.verify-fix.*`, `agent.pickup` |
| `triager` | Triager | PROJECT | `*.read`, `comment.create`, `comment.update.own`, `comment.delete.own`, `ticket.update`, `ticket.assign`, `ticket.transition.verify`, `ticket.transition.reject`, `ticket.label.*`, `label.create`, `agent.pickup` |
| `approver` | Approver | PROJECT | `*.read`, `approval.decide` |
| `viewer` | Viewer | PROJECT | `*.read`, `comment.create`, `comment.update.own`, `comment.delete.own`, `ticket.watch.*` |

**`SystemRoleSeeder`** is an `OnApplicationBootstrap` provider in `PermissionsModule`. It reads its seed list from the injection token `SYSTEM_ROLES_SEED`, which `PermissionsModule` provides as `SYSTEM_ROLES`, so tests can supply another list.

The seeded `agent` role leaves out the design's `mcp.access`, because `mcp.access` is an implicit key every authenticated principal holds and cannot appear in a role.

The seeder:
- Before any write, it validates every seeded role with `expandEntries`. An invalid entry throws, and the API does not start.
- It then upserts each role by `key`.
- A missing role is created.
- A **locked** role whose stored `permissions`, `name` or `scope` differ is overwritten with the seed.
- An unlocked system role keeps its stored `permissions`, because admins may edit them. Its `name` and `scope` are reset to the seed.
- It never deletes a row.

Module/persistence rulings:
1. **All new code lives in `apps/api/src/permissions/`** as `PermissionsModule`.
   - It is `@Global()`. It exports only `PermissionService`, `MembershipService` and `RoleAdminService`.
   - Its repositories (ruling 6) are module-private and are the only code that touches `Role` or `RoleBinding` through Prisma.
   - Every consumer injects the services without `@Optional()`.
6. **Repositories follow `.nax/rules/api-data.md`.**
   - `PrismaRoleRepository` and `PrismaRoleBindingRepository` each extend `AbstractPrismaRepository` from `@nathapp/nestjs-prisma`.
   - Their domain types are `RoleDomain` and `RoleBindingDomain`, plain interfaces.
   - Each is registered behind a symbol token: `ROLE_REPOSITORY`, `ROLE_BINDING_REPOSITORY`.
   - Escape-hatch methods (row locks, `User.role` writes, user and agent existence checks) live on the concrete classes.
9. **Test setup.** `test/helpers/reset-db.ts` truncates every table, so a test that needs the system roles runs `SystemRoleSeeder.onApplicationBootstrap()` after the reset, or boots the app.

Add PermissionsModule to AppModule imports. This story creates the shell and seeder; only export public services as they become available in dependent stories, never repositories or unimplemented imports. Keep seed writes compatible with the permissions tag invalidation contract introduced in US-003.

**Scope** — In: schema, migration, two partial indexes, two repositories and domain interfaces, tokens, seed data, bootstrap provider and module registration. Out: evaluation/membership services (US-003), agent cleanup caller integration (US-004), RoleAdminService and controllers (US-005/006), copying or dropping legacy tables.

**Interface** — `SYSTEM_ROLES`, `SYSTEM_ROLES_SEED`, `ROLE_REPOSITORY`, `ROLE_BINDING_REPOSITORY`; `SystemRoleSeeder.onApplicationBootstrap(): Promise<void>`; plain `RoleDomain` and `RoleBindingDomain` matching the schema values without exposing generated Prisma types.
acceptanceCriteria: [integration] After application bootstrap on an empty test database, Role contains exactly owner, admin, member, agent, project-admin, developer, reviewer, verifier, triager, approver and viewer, each with system true.
[integration] After bootstrap, owner is the only Role with locked true.
[integration] A second bootstrap on the same database creates no new Role rows.
[integration] When developer.permissions was set to ['ticket.read'] before a second bootstrap, its permissions remain ['ticket.read'] afterwards.
[integration] When owner.permissions was set to ['ticket.read'] before a second bootstrap, its permissions become ['*'] afterwards.
[unit] SystemRoleSeeder.onApplicationBootstrap given a seed containing no.such.key rejects with UnknownPermissionEntryError before any repository write.
[integration] Given a seeded role with an invalid permission entry, application bootstrap rejects rather than starting the API.
[integration] Inserting a second RoleBinding with identical principalType, principalId and roleId and null projectId fails with a unique violation.
[integration] Inserting a second RoleBinding with identical principalType, principalId, roleId and non-null projectId fails with a unique violation.
[integration] Hard-deleting a Project deletes its RoleBinding rows by cascade.
[integration] Deleting a Role referenced by a RoleBinding fails with a foreign key violation.

routing.reasoning: New private persistence abstractions, PostgreSQL partial indexes and security role seeding require real database and bootstrap behavior; security override applies.

suggestedCriteria: When an unlocked system role's stored name or scope differs from its seed, a second bootstrap resets name and scope while preserving stored permissions.
When the last role in SYSTEM_ROLES_SEED is invalid, SystemRoleSeeder leaves previously missing valid roles uncreated.
When a custom non-system role exists, SystemRoleSeeder leaves that row unchanged.

modifiedFiles.reason: PARTIAL_UNIQUE_INDEXES gains the two RoleBinding statements. The invariant: every entry matches a migration statement verbatim.
AppModule adds PermissionsModule to its imports, so the seeder runs at bootstrap and the global services resolve.

userStories.title: PermissionService and MembershipService
acceptanceCriteria: [integration] Given a user with developer in p1, PermissionService.can(user, 'ticket.create', { projectId: p1 }) returns { allowed: true, reason: 'granted' }.
[integration] Given the same developer user, can(user, 'ticket.delete', { projectId: p1 }) returns { allowed: false, reason: 'not-granted' }.
[integration] Given the same user has no binding in p2, can(user, 'ticket.create', { projectId: p2 }) returns allowed false.
[integration] Given an agent with a projectId-null reviewer binding, can(agent, 'ticket.transition.close', { projectId: p2 }) returns allowed true although the agent has no binding in p2.
[integration] Given a user with a projectId-null admin binding, can(user, 'user.create') returns allowed true.
[integration] Given that admin user, can(user, 'role.binding.owner') returns allowed false.
[integration] Given a user with no bindings and legacy User.role 'ADMIN', can(user, 'user.create') returns allowed true.
[integration] Given a user with no bindings, can(user, 'notification.read') returns { allowed: true, reason: 'implicit' }.
[integration] Given a user with no bindings, can(user, 'ticket.create', {}) returns { allowed: false, reason: 'no-project' }.
[integration] Given an agent with a projectId-null owner binding inserted directly, can(agent, 'role.binding.owner') returns { allowed: false, reason: 'principal-type' }.
[integration] Given a runner principal, can(runner, 'ticket.read', { projectId: p1 }) returns allowed false.
[integration] Given a user with viewer in p1, can(user, 'comment.update', { projectId: p1, resource: { createdBy: { type: 'USER', id: user.id } } }) returns allowed true.

[integration] Given that viewer user and another user's createdBy.id, can(user, 'comment.update', { projectId: p1, resource: { createdBy: { type: 'USER', id: otherUser.id } } }) returns { allowed: false, reason: 'not-owner' }.
[integration] Given that viewer user with no resource context, can(user, 'comment.update', { projectId: p1 }) returns reason 'not-owner'.

[integration] After can(user, 'ticket.create', { projectId: p1 }) returned allowed true, removing the developer binding with MembershipService.removeBinding makes the next identical can call return allowed false.

[integration] Two concurrent MembershipService.createBinding calls for identical principal, roleKey and projectId resolve to RoleBindingViews with the same id and exactly one persisted RoleBinding row.
[integration] Creating a projectId-null admin binding for a user through MembershipService stores User.role 'ADMIN'.
[integration] After creating that admin binding, MembershipService.isGlobalAdmin(userId) returns true.
[integration] Removing the user's only projectId-null admin binding stores User.role 'MEMBER'.
[integration] After removing that only admin binding, MembershipService.isGlobalAdmin(userId) returns false.
[integration] MembershipService.removeBinding of the only owner binding rejects with ForbiddenAppException carrying permissions.ownerLocked, leaving the binding in place.
[integration] With exactly two owner bindings, concurrent removeBinding calls leave exactly one binding, with one fulfilled call and one rejection carrying permissions.ownerLocked.

routing.reasoning: Authorization evaluation, legacy compatibility, real PostgreSQL races, owner row locks, cache coherence and token revocation are cross-cutting security architecture.

suggestedCriteria: PermissionService.can(user, 'no.such.key') returns { allowed: false, reason: 'unknown-key' }.
PermissionService.can(user, 'session.login') returns { allowed: true, reason: 'public' }.
Given a global admin binding, effectiveKeys(userRef, 'global') contains ticket.create, role.binding.manage and approval.policy.manage.
Given only one enabled-user Owner binding and a second binding belonging to a disabled user, removing the enabled-user Owner rejects with permissions.ownerLocked.
When a binding write changes User.role, that user's tokenVersion increments once and previously issued access and refresh tokens are rejected.
setGlobalAdmin(userId, false, by) preserves the user's owner binding and User.role 'ADMIN' when that user also has an admin binding.
setGlobalAdmin(userId, false, by) stores User.role 'MEMBER' for a legacy ADMIN without owner or admin bindings.
When listBindings is called without a page option, it returns current 1, size 50 and at most 50 records.
When a binding transaction rolls back, the next effectiveKeys call does not include the rolled-back grant.

userStories.title: Owner bootstrap and baseline bindings
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Connect registration, admin-user management and agent lifecycle to MembershipService with canonical Owner email bootstrap.

**Motivation** — The user ruled (2026-10-18) that these gaps are fixed by one redesign: one permission catalog, roles as data, and one binding model for users and agents.

**Approach** — Owner bootstrap and baseline bindings
- **`IAuthConfig.ownerEmail`** is read from `KODA_OWNER_EMAIL`. `authConfig` trims and lower-cases the raw value **before** validation: it validates a copy of `process.env` whose `KODA_OWNER_EMAIL` is already trimmed and lower-cased. `AuthConfigSchema` gains `@IsOptional() @IsEmail() KODA_OWNER_EMAIL?: string`. An empty value after trimming is mapped to `undefined` in that copy, so it counts as unset.
- **Production check.** `PermissionsModule.onModuleInit` throws `Error('permissions.ownerEmailRequired')` when `NODE_ENV === 'production'` and `ownerEmail` is unset.
- **Registration.**
  - `AuthService.register` refuses before creating the user, with `ForbiddenAppException({}, 'registration')`, when:
    - the users table is empty,
    - `ownerEmail` is set, and
    - the canonical email differs from it.
  - After creating the user, it calls:
    - `MembershipService.bindOwnerIfFirst(userId, wasFirstUser)`. `wasFirstUser` is the `firstUser` flag that `PrismaAuthRepository.findAnyUserAndCreate` already returns, as `{ user, firstUser }`. That method keeps storing `role: 'ADMIN'` for the first user, unchanged.
    - `MembershipService.bindBaseline({ type: 'USER', id })`.
- **Admin user routes.**
  - `UsersAdminService.create(dto)` calls `bindBaseline`. When `dto.role` is `ADMIN`, it also calls `setGlobalAdmin(id, true, { type: 'SYSTEM', id: 'admin-users' })`.
  - `UsersAdminService.update(actorId, userId, patch)` with `patch.role` calls `setGlobalAdmin(userId, patch.role === 'ADMIN', { type: 'USER', id: actorId })` instead of writing `role` through `repo.updateUser`.
  - The existing last-admin guard keeps counting with `countActiveAdmins`. That still reads `User.role`, which `setGlobalAdmin` keeps in step.
- **Agents.** `AgentsService.generateApiKey(dto)`, the create path behind `POST /agents`, calls `bindBaseline({ type: 'AGENT', id })` inside its existing transaction.

Required integration targets:
- `UsersAdminService.update` with a changed `role` goes through `MembershipService.setGlobalAdmin`, which now does the `tokenVersion` bump and cache invalidation for the role change. `update` keeps doing them itself for `disabled`.
- `MembershipService` is a required constructor parameter, inserted as the **fourth** parameter after `txManager` and before the two `@Optional()` ones: `(agentRepo, authConfig, txManager, membership, kodaDomainWriter?, agentAuthProvider?)`.
- Agent deletion (`AgentsService.remove(slug)`, behind `DELETE /agents/:slug`) calls `MembershipService.removeAllBindings({ type: 'AGENT', id })`.
- Users are never deleted, only disabled. Their bindings stay, and later readers check `disabled`.

`setGlobalAdmin(userId, false, by)` removes only the global admin binding, never owner. Return the actual stored user role after membership operations: owner+admin demotion leaves owner and legacy ADMIN; a legacy ADMIN without bindings becomes MEMBER. Keep existing last-admin/self protections, disabled handling, legacy agent role/capability writes and agent auth invalidations. No optional membership injection is permitted.

userStories.title: Roles API
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Expose bounded role listing and guarded role CRUD through RoleAdminService with localized failures and exported OpenAPI operations.

**Motivation** — Roles and bindings must exist, and be manageable, before any check can move onto them.

**Approach** — REST and authorization rulings
4. **The new routes do not use the legacy decorators.** They call `PermissionService` through `RoleAdminService.assertCan`, instead of `@RequiredPermission` or `@ProjectPermission`, which `.nax/rules/api-core.md` would otherwise require.
   - This is a deliberate, scoped exception. These routes are the first ones on the new model, and the legacy CASL factory has no notion of roles or bindings.
   - Every other `.nax/rules/api-controllers.md` convention still applies: the JSON envelope, `@ApiTags`, `@ApiBearerAuth`, `@ApiOperation`, `@ApiResponse`, `@ApiProperty` on every response DTO field, and app exceptions.
5. **i18n and exceptions.**
   - Every new message lives in the new files `apps/api/src/i18n/en/permissions.json` and `apps/api/src/i18n/zh/permissions.json`, with English as the source.
   - A code written in this spec as `permissions.<code>` with status `<s>` means `new <XAppException>({}, 'permissions.<code>')` from `@nathapp/nestjs-common` where exported; for ConflictAppException reuse the existing `apps/api/src/common/exceptions/conflict-app.exception.ts`, which supplies the same 409/prefix semantics because the package does not export it. Its message lives at the nested i18n key `permissions.<code>.<s>`, the shape of `users.json` with `lastAdmin.409`.
   - A bare `permissions` 403 means `new ForbiddenAppException({}, 'permissions')`, with its message at `permissions.403`.
   - Each code's exception class and status are given in "Failure Handling".
7. **Bounded reads.**
   - `Role` is a small, admin-written table. `GET /roles` reads it with `take: 500`.
8. **Order of checks on every new write route:**
   1. the route's permission key(s) (`assertCan`);
   2. input validation and lookups (DTO, role, project, principal, scope match, principal type);
   3. self-binding;
   4. escalation;
   5. Owner lock.

   The first failing step decides the response.

All routes take the global prefix and return the JSON envelope. Each route's check runs through `RoleAdminService.assertCan(principal, key, projectId?)`, which throws `ForbiddenAppException('permissions')` when `can` denies.

| Route | Key checked | Body / result |
|:--|:--|:--|
| `GET /roles` | `role.read` | `RoleDto[]` = `{ id, key, name, description, scope, system, locked, permissions }` |
| `POST /roles` | `role.manage` | `{ key, name, description?, scope, permissions }` → 201 `RoleDto` |
| `PATCH /roles/:id` | `role.manage` | `{ name?, description?, permissions? }` → 200 `RoleDto` |
| `DELETE /roles/:id` | `role.manage` | 204 |

**Role write rules** (`RoleAdminService`):
- **Validation.** `permissions` must pass `expandEntries(permissions, scope)`. A failure answers 400 `ValidationAppException('permissions.unknownEntry')` or `('permissions.scopeMismatch')`.
- **Escalation.** Every key in `expandEntries(permissions, scope)`, with `X.own` counted as `X` and `approval.decide@…` counted as `approval.decide`, must be in the caller's `effectiveKeys(caller, 'global')`. Otherwise 403 `permissions.escalation`. This applies to POST and PATCH only.
- **Deleting a role** has no escalation check, because deleting a role grants nothing. Its checks run in the order: locked, then system role, then in use.
- **Duplicate key.** `POST /roles` with an existing `key` answers 409 `permissions.roleKeyTaken`. A concurrent duplicate insert, caught with `isUniqueViolation(error, 'key')`, answers the same.
- **Input format.**
  - `key` must match `^[a-z][a-z0-9-]{1,48}$`.
  - `scope` must be `GLOBAL` or `PROJECT`.
  - Both are checked by the DTO; a violation answers the standard 400 validation response.
  - An empty `permissions` list is allowed.
- **Fixed fields.** `key` and `scope` cannot change. PATCH accepts no such fields.
- **System roles.** PATCH on a system role may change only `permissions` and `description`. A `name` in the body answers 400 `ValidationAppException('permissions.systemRole')`.
- **Locked roles.** PATCH or DELETE on a locked role answers 403 `ForbiddenAppException('permissions.ownerLocked')`.
- **Deleting.**
  - DELETE on an unlocked system role answers 403 `permissions.systemRole`.
  - DELETE on a role with bindings answers 409 `permissions.roleInUse`.

**Role delete race.** A foreign key violation on `RoleBinding.roleId` during a role delete, from a binding inserted concurrently, is mapped to 409 `permissions.roleInUse`.
**Unknown ids.** `PATCH` or `DELETE /roles/:id` with an unknown id answers 404 `permissions.roleNotFound`.

Failure classes: unknownEntry/scopeMismatch/systemRole-name are ValidationAppException 400; escalation/ownerLocked/systemRole-delete/bare permissions are ForbiddenAppException 403; roleKeyTaken/roleInUse are ConflictAppException 409; roleNotFound is NotFoundAppException 404. All messages use nested status keys in both new locales. Every Role write invalidates the permissions cache tag in this service call; cache correctness includes the immediate next PermissionService.can result. RoleAdminService uses private repositories for role persistence and PermissionService for decisions; no controller accesses Prisma. Register/export RoleAdminService in PermissionsModule, leaving repository tokens private.

Regenerate root openapi.json using bun run api:export-spec, not CLI generation. Extend test/e2e/api-endpoint/endpoint.e2e.spec.ts with a happy path and one error for each /roles route, existing cases unchanged. Swagger completeness is checked by integration/openapi-spec/spec-integrity.integration.spec.ts. Registration-to-role.read AC15 is a full-feature seam with sibling US-004, not an upstream dependency of this story. Preserve the fixed graph and test actual POST /auth/register followed by GET /roles once both stories are assembled; direct binding fixtures, mocks or skipped assertions do not satisfy that AC. Bootstrap implementation stays in US-004.

**Scope** — In: RoleAdminService, RolesController, role DTOs, English/Chinese permission messages, role CRUD guards, permission cache invalidation and OpenAPI/e2e integration. Out: registration callers (US-004), binding management routes (US-006), legacy permission migration, CLI/web generation, rate limits beyond global throttler; approval policies, floors and approval.decide enforcement (P3), and action context/audit rows (P2). Only permission metadata is represented here.

**Interface** — `RoleAdminService.assertCan(principal: KodaPrincipal, key: string, projectId?: string): Promise<void>`; `RoleDto` fields `{ id, key, name, description, scope, system, locked, permissions }`; create body `{ key, name, description?, scope, permissions }`; patch body `{ name?, description?, permissions? }`. PermissionService interfaces consumed verbatim:
```ts
can(principal: KodaPrincipal, key: string,
    ctx?: { projectId?: string; resource?: { createdBy: PrincipalRef | null } }): Promise<PermissionDecision>;
effectiveKeys(principal: PrincipalRef, scope: { projectId: string } | 'global'): Promise<ReadonlySet<string>>;
```

analysis:
Existing-system enhancement, not greenfield. Goal: add the permission catalog, role and binding persistence, system seeds, evaluation and administration services, lifecycle bootstrap and REST management without migrating existing authorization. Exactly six stories retain the supplied dependency graph; US-004 and US-005 may follow US-003 independently, and US-006 follows US-005. All runtime additions belong under apps/api/src/permissions except the explicitly specified schema, configuration, lifecycle integration, i18n and test edits. The final @Global PermissionsModule exports only PermissionService, MembershipService and RoleAdminService; repositories and their tokens remain private. Services are required injections, never @Optional. Read .nax/mono/apps/api/context.md and the nathapp-nestjs-patterns skill before implementation; that skill was not present among repository files available during this analysis. Graph-first navigation could not be used because codebase-memory tools were unavailable, so findings below come from direct reads and targeted searches.

Verified architecture: auto-detected Express metadata is misleading for production: apps/api/src/main.ts:12 uses AppFactory.createFastifyApp, installs CombinedAuthGuard before app init at :38-48, and sets prefix/pipes/filters/guards. apps/api/package.json:43-83 has NestJS 12, Prisma 7 and Nathapp ~4.1 packages, including nestjs-auth ~4.1.1; older guidance mentioning auth v3 must not cause a dependency downgrade. No new dependency is needed. AppModule already registers a global transaction-enabled PrismaModule at apps/api/src/app.module.ts:84-91 and global CacheStrategy.MEMORY at :93-100. Insert PermissionsModule in its imports. apps/api/src/auth/principal/koda-principal.types.ts:8-38 defines actorType user/agent/runner and the USER/AGENT reference conversion must use these actual shapes, not infer user status from id. Existing projectRole and agentRoles remain untouched. apps/api/src/common/enums.ts:7 demonstrates local const/type style; do not introduce Prisma enums.

Catalog and grammar: apps/api/src/permissions currently does not exist. docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-18-permission-action-inventory.tsv:1 names proposed_key and catalog_scope; rows can repeat a key and contain semicolon-delimited keys. Aggregate all rows per key before scope derivation; do not derive scope from the first route. agent.read occurs globally and in projects at :3-5. codeintel.read is global at :20-23 whereas codeintel.impact.read is project at :182; wildcards must filter by fitting keys. Workspace creation/read/send/archive rows at :128-133 and memory creation/extraction/decision rows at :149-151 need the exact ownability overrides. Build a code-owned catalog, not a runtime dependency on a TSV file shipped with docs. Test catalog parity against the inventory. Preserve first-match ordering for access and risk, implicit/public exclusion from grants, wildcard/exclusion behavior, own-only variants and approval.decide@ patterns. Approval metadata is descriptive only.

Persistence and seeds: apps/api/prisma/schema.prisma:156-201 contains Project and its relation list; add roleBindings plus Role/RoleBinding with string scopes and polymorphic principalId without a principal FK. Existing ProjectMember, AgentProject, AgentRoleEntry and User.role remain. No production data migration/backfill: create tables and indexes only. Ship apps/api/prisma/migrations/20261027090000_role_bindings/migration.sql and regenerate the ignored Prisma client. apps/api/test/helpers/partial-indexes.ts:6-13 currently contains six indexes; append the two specified SQL strings verbatim. apps/api/test/unit/fleet/partial-indexes.spec.ts:5-16 compares every helper string to migration text, so PostgreSQL null uniqueness must be provided in both places. Role FK restricts deletion; Project hard-delete cascades binding cleanup, though normal project deletion remains soft-delete. .nax/rules/api-data.md:19-42 and :108-150 require AbstractPrismaRepository, plain domain mappings and symbol-token registration; use generated client types only in persistence layers. Existing apps/api/src/memory/memory.module.ts:36-39 shows useExisting token wiring, but its repository exports at :45-49 are legacy and must not be copied. Seeder validation must finish for the entire injected SYSTEM_ROLES_SEED before its first write. Seed all eleven roles, preserve editable stored permissions, repair owner permissions and seeded name/scope, and invalidate permission cache on writes once services are installed. Module shell is staged: do not reference not-yet-created downstream service files in US-002.

Evaluation and membership: apps/api/src/auth/jwt-auth.provider.ts:43-56 shows CacheManager.get(key, loader, 60_000, { tags }); :60-65 derives revocation from cached DB state while role itself stays a JWT claim. Effective keys must combine global roles, project/global PROJECT roles, the persisted legacy ADMIN union and explicit global Owner/Admin project wildcard augmentation, including in effectiveKeys(..., 'global') for escalation. Route checks deny project keys without a project even for Owner. No existing guard/check is replaced. All Role/RoleBinding writes invalidate permissions in the same service call. Important runtime risk: apps/api/src/auth/auth.service.ts:134-141 and apps/api/src/users/users-admin.service.ts:73-78 explicitly document that MEMORY tag invalidation has no registry and evict the direct auth-state key too. Verify the installed cache implementation and ensure permission cache entries are invalidated after writes rather than assuming a tag call suffices; retain the specified CacheManager/tag/TTL contract without prescribing an unverified new helper or adding Redis. Always make post-write calls observe the latest committed state. Repositories alone handle SQL locks, principal/project existence and User.role writes. Use TRANSACTION_MANAGER transparent transactions, not threaded tx handles or callback $transaction. apps/api/src/common/utils/prisma-errors.ts:9-16 uses getUniqueConstraintTarget and substring matching; duplicate bindings use isUniqueViolation(error, 'principalId'), duplicate roles use 'key', never error.meta.target. Recover uniqueness races outside an aborted transaction boundary or with a conflict-safe insert so the re-read can succeed on PostgreSQL. Serialize Owner binding changes with SELECT FOR UPDATE on the owner Role row, count enabled-user owners only, and keep count/delete atomic. Concurrent admin mirroring also needs atomic re-read of remaining owner/admin bindings. outOfScope: Moving any existing route, guard or tool check (`@RequiredPermission`, `@ProjectPermission`, `@ProjectRoles`, `exemptAgents`, `requireUser`, `assertUser`, tool `permission.kind`) onto permission keys is out of scope (`permissions-p1-enforce-core`, `permissions-p1-enforce-fleet`). No existing permission decision changes, except that global admin bindings are mirrored into `User.role`.
Invalidating the cached agent principal (`AGENT:<id>` tags) on binding writes is out of scope (`permissions-p1-membership`). Agent principals do not read bindings in this feature.

A live JWT `role` read from bindings on every request is out of scope (`permissions-p1-membership`). In this feature a change to a user's global admin status revokes their tokens (see `MembershipService` rules), so their next login carries the new `role` claim, as today.
Dropping `ProjectMember`, `AgentProject`, `AgentRoleEntry`, `User.role` or `ProjectInvite.role` is out of scope (`permissions-p1-cleanup`).
Copying existing membership data into bindings is out of scope (no data migration; koda-wk is reset by hand).
Approval policies, floors and `approval.decide` enforcement are out of scope (design phase P3). The catalog `approval` fields are placeholders.
Action context and audit rows are out of scope (design phase P2). Bindings record only `grantedByType` and `grantedById`.
Regenerating the CLI client in `apps/cli/src/generated/` is out of scope; no CLI command uses the new routes yet. Only the repo-root `openapi.json` is updated.
Web pages for roles and bindings are out of scope (`permissions-p1-web`).

US-005 only: rate limits on the new routes beyond the global throttler are out of scope.
